title: Enhancing Low-Resource Language Reasoning via High-Resource Language Feature Transfer
abstract: arXiv:2608.30462v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models exhibit substantial performance variation across languages, even when solving semantically equivalent tasks. Existing analyses often treat this phenomenon as an observational disparity caused by differences in pretraining data, tokenization, or benchmark coverage. We study a complementary hypothesis: high-resource languages (HRLs) may more reliably elicit latent computations useful for task-specific (i.e. mathematical) reasoning, while lower-resource languages (LRLs) may under-activate those computations despite expressing the same task. To test this hypothesis, we introduce a mechanistic intervention framework for identifying and transferring task-relevant sparse latent features across languages. Using sparse autoencoders over residual-stream activations, we isolate features enriched in successful HRL task-specific reasoning while filtering out source-language and generic-generation features. translated_title: 通过高资源语言特征迁移增强低资源语言推理能力
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型在不同语言上表现出显著的性能差异，即使是在解决语义等价的任务时也是如此。现有分析通常将这一现象视为由预训练数据、分词或基准覆盖范围差异所导致的观测性差异。我们研究了另一个互补的假设：高资源语言（HRL）可能更可靠地激发对任务特定（即数学）推理有用的潜在计算，而低资源语言（LRL）尽管表达了相同的任务，却可能未能充分激活这些计算。为验证这一假设，我们引入了一个机制性干预框架，用于识别并在语言之间迁移与任务相关的稀疏潜在特征。利用基于残差流激活的稀疏自编码器，我们分离出在成功的高资源语言任务特定推理中富集的特征，同时过滤掉源语言特征和通用生成特征。随后我们构建了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一个基于稀疏自编码器的机制性干预框架，通过识别并迁移高资源语言中与数学推理相关的稀疏潜在特征到低资源语言，从而提升低资源语言的任务推理能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a mechanistic intervention framework that uses sparse autoencoders to identify and transfer task-relevant sparse latent features from high-resource languages to low-resource languages, thereby enhancing task-specific reasoning performance in low-resource languages.
